callChain: RocketMQ customizer sets consumeThreadNumber and consumeThreadMax to the configured value
each consumer thread synchronously reads task/comment and conditionally claims execution ownership
the same thread performs blocking RestClient AI HTTP using SimpleClientHttpRequestFactory
saveSuccess transaction conditionally marks SUCCESS, inserts one analysis_result row, then commits
no shared global lock or single result-persistence scheduler exists in this path

conclusion.c2ToC4: Consumer concurrency is the limiting downstream factor at c2; c4 nearly doubles throughput and materially reduces inflight backlog.
conclusion.c4ToC8: c8 still improves throughput, but scaling efficiency drops and inflight nearly disappears.
conclusion.newLimit: At c8, throughput and persistence rate converge on the roughly 35-40 events/s Outbox publishing supply, so the limiting boundary moves back to the publisher side.
conclusion.batch100Value: Batch size 100 is useful only when consumer concurrency is high enough to use the additional supply; it did not help c2 in Phase 5 but unlocks c4/c8 scaling here.
conclusion.nextOptimization: Optimize the sequential Outbox claim -> syncSend -> mark-sent dispatch path with bounded pipelining while preserving conditional state transitions and retry semantics.

resumeSafe.caveat: single-machine local environment, deterministic 100ms HTTP AI Stub, batch size 100; no real BERT/LLM
